# Arithmetic functions on nonzero ideals

For the intended number-field applications, an ideal-indexed Dirichlet series should not assign an
arithmetic coefficient to the zero ideal. Excluding it ensures that ideal convolution never
considers factorizations through the zero ideal. This file introduces the carrier used throughout
the arithmetic-Dirichlet-series roadmap, parameterized over an arbitrary field:

* `TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction K` is a complex-valued function on the nonzero ideals of
  `𝓞 K`;
* `TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.zeroExtend` is its canonical extension to all integral ideals,
  with value zero at the zero ideal;
* `TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.restrict` restricts a function on all ideals to the nonzero
  ideals;
* `TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.map` and `TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.mapEquiv`:
  functoriality under an isomorphism `K ≃+* L` of the ambient fields.

It also carries the multiplicativity predicate
`TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.IsMultiplicative` — value `1` at the unit ideal, multiplicative on
relatively prime nonzero ideals — together with its two factorization consequences:
`IsMultiplicative.map_prod` for a pairwise relatively prime finite product, and, over a number
field, `IsMultiplicative.map_prod_pow` for a prime-power factorization of a nonzero ideal, the
factorizations themselves being supplied by `Ideal.exists_eq_prod_pow`.

The two operations are inverse precisely on functions vanishing at the zero ideal. The resulting
existence-and-uniqueness API is recorded without exposing the implementation of `zeroExtend`:
`TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.existsUnique_zeroExtend_eq` characterizes its image, while
`TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.zeroExtend_injective` says that no information is lost.

The extension respects the pointwise additive, scalar, and multiplicative operations. It does not
preserve the pointwise unit: the constant-one function on all ideals takes value one at the zero
ideal, and therefore cannot be a zero extension. The theorem
`TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.not_exists_zeroExtend_eq_one` is the zero-ideal rejection test
required by Layer 0 of the roadmap.

## Roadmap role

This is Layer **0.1** of `TauCetiRoadmap/ArithmeticDirichletSeries/README.md`, and is the common
carrier on which its norm regrouping, ideal convolution, Euler products, and summatory functions
are built. Later Layer 0 files add completely multiplicative and unitary subtypes; those are
special coefficient systems on this general carrier, not replacements for it.

## References

* `TauCetiRoadmap/ArithmeticDirichletSeries/Suggested.lean`, whose Layer 0.1 nonzero-ideal
  carrier and zero-extension design are adapted here.
* J. Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, Chapter VII.
* G. Tenenbaum, *Introduction to Analytic and Probabilistic Number Theory*, Chapters II--III.

# The ideal von Mangoldt function

The von Mangoldt function of a nonzero ideal `A` of the ring of integers of a number field is
`log N(P)` when `A` is a positive power of a prime ideal `P`, and zero otherwise.  This file
packages that function as an `IdealArithmeticFunction` and defines its pointwise product with an
ideal arithmetic function.

## Main definitions

* `TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt` is the complex-valued ideal von Mangoldt
  function.
* `TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldtTransform` sends `f` to the weighted function
  `A ↦ f(A) Λ(A)`.

## Main results

* `TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt_apply_prime_pow` computes the value on a positive
  power of a prime ideal.
* `TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt_ne_zero_iff` says that its support is exactly the
  prime-power ideals.
* `TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldtTransform_ne_zero_iff` identifies the support of
  the transform, and its specialization in `TauCeti.MultiplicativeIdealWeight` describes this as
  the good prime powers for a completely multiplicative weight.

The definition chooses a prime base from a proof that `A` is a prime power.  Mathlib's
`eq_of_prime_pow_eq`, applied to ideals, identifies that choice with any prime base supplied by a
caller.  The public evaluation theorem therefore removes the choice from every computation.

## Implementation notes

This is the ideal analogue of Mathlib's `ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt`.  Here the prime base is
chosen from `IsPrimePow` rather than computed by `Nat.minFac`, its logarithmic weight is
`Ideal.absNorm P` rather than `p`, and the function is complex-valued to match
`IdealArithmeticFunction`.

## Roadmap role

This is the algebraic part of Layer **2.3** of
`TauCetiRoadmap/ArithmeticDirichletSeries/README.md`.  The logarithmic-derivative identity named in
that target additionally requires the Euler-product package of Layer 3; this file supplies its
coefficient and exact prime-power support in advance.

## References

* J. Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, Chapter VII.
* G. Tenenbaum, *Introduction to Analytic and Probabilistic Number Theory*, Chapter I.2.

# Natural density of sets of prime ideals

For a number field `K`, this file defines the natural density of a set `S` of nonzero prime
ideals as the limit

```text
  primeCount K S x / primeCount K Set.univ x
```

as the inclusive real cutoff `x` tends to infinity. This normalization matches Mathlib's
ratio-normalized `NumberField.Set.HasDirichletDensity`: a density is measured relative to all
prime ideals of the same number field, rather than relative to an external approximation such as
`x / log x`.

The denominator really tends to infinity. Indeed, lying over supplies a prime of `𝓞 K` above
every rational prime, so the height-one spectrum is infinite. Its bounded-norm subsets are finite
and exhaust the spectrum, whence their cardinalities tend to infinity. This fact both makes the
whole spectrum have density one and ensures that a fixed finite error disappears in the ratio.

## Main results

* `NumberField.Set.HasNaturalDensity`: ratio-normalized natural density for a set of prime ideals.
* `NumberField.Set.hasNaturalDensity_def`: the defining ratio-convergence characterization.
* `NumberField.Set.HasNaturalDensity.union`,
  `NumberField.Set.hasNaturalDensity_biUnion_finset` and
  `NumberField.Set.HasNaturalDensity.compl`: finite Boolean calculus for natural density.
* `NumberField.Set.HasNaturalDensity.of_finite_symmDiff`: changing a prime set on finitely many
  primes preserves its natural density.
* `NumberField.Set.hasNaturalDensity_of_finite`: every finite set of prime ideals has natural
  density zero.
* `NumberField.Set.isUpperDirichletDensityBound_of_eventually_primeCount_le` and
  `NumberField.Set.isLowerDirichletDensityBound_of_eventually_le_primeCount`: an eventual
  one-sided bound on the proportion of primes of `S` below `x` is the same one-sided bound for
  Dirichlet density.
* `NumberField.Set.hasDirichletDensity_of_hasNaturalDensity`: natural density implies Dirichlet
  density, with the same value.

The comparison with Dirichlet density rests on two inputs. Abel summation against the decreasing
function `t ↦ t ^ (-s)` (`TauCeti.tsum_mul_le_of_summatory_le`) turns an eventual bound
`π_S(x) ≤ c · π(x)` into a bound `P_S(s) ≤ c · P(s) + C` with `C` independent of `s > 1`, where
`P_S` is Mathlib's `NumberField.Set.primeIdealZetaSum S`. The all-prime sum `P(s)` tends to
infinity as `s → 1⁺` (`TauCeti.tendsto_primeIdealZetaSum_univ_atTop`), so the constant `C`
disappears from the ratio `P_S(s) / P(s)`.

The definition, its elementary calculus, and the comparison with Dirichlet density are standard;
see J.-P. Serre, *A Course in Arithmetic*, Chapter VI, §4, J.-P. Serre, *Corps locaux*, Chapter
VI, or J. Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, Chapter VII, §13.

# The completely split primes as the identity Artin fibre

Let `L / K` be a finite Galois extension of number fields. Among the fibres of the Artin class
studied in `TauCeti.NumberTheory.Chebotarev.FrobeniusPrimeSet`, the fibre of the identity class
`1` is distinguished: it consists exactly of the primes of `𝓞 K` that split completely in `L`.

Two readings of membership in `frobeniusPrimeSet K L 1` are recorded. The residue-degree reading
asks for a prime `𝔭` unramified in `L`, and says that `f(Q/𝔭)` is `1` at one — hence, since
`L / K` is Galois, at every — prime `Q` of `𝓞 L` above `𝔭`. The counting reading needs no
hypothesis at all: `𝔭` carries the identity Artin class exactly when `𝓞 L` has the full
complement of `[L : K]` primes above `𝔭`.

That asymmetry is the point of the file. A full complement of primes above `𝔭` already forces
the ramification index at every prime above `𝔭` to be `1`, hence forces `𝔭` to be unramified —
that is `NumberField.isUnramifiedAt_of_ncard_primesOver_eq_finrank`, in
`TauCeti.NumberTheory.NumberField.SplitsCompletely.Basic`. So the counting characterization and its
set-level corollary both stand unconditionally, and `frobeniusPrimeSet K L 1` is the set of
completely split primes on the nose, with no finite exceptional set to discard.

## Main results

* `NumberField.Chebotarev.mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_one_iff_inertiaDeg_eq_one`: for `𝔭` unramified
  in `L`, membership in the identity fibre is residue degree one at a prime above `𝔭`.
* `NumberField.Chebotarev.mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_one_iff_ncard_primesOver_eq_finrank`: the same
  membership, read as a count of the primes above `𝔭`.
* `NumberField.Chebotarev.inertiaDeg_eq_one_of_mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_one`: a member of the
  identity fibre has residue degree one at *every* prime above it.
* `NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPrimeSet_one_eq_setOf_ncard_primesOver_eq_finrank`: as a set,
  the identity fibre is the primes of `𝓞 K` with `[L : K]` primes of `𝓞 L` above them.

## References

* J. Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, Chapter I, §9, where the Frobenius at an unramified
  prime is trivial exactly when that prime splits completely.

# The unramified primes carrying a prescribed Artin class

Let `L / K` be a finite Galois extension of number fields and let `C` be a conjugacy class in
`Gal(L/K)`. This file defines the set

`frobeniusPrimeSet K L C : Set (HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K))`

of height-one primes `𝔭` of `𝓞 K` that are unramified in `L` and whose Artin class is `C`. It is
the set whose density the Chebotarev density theorem computes.

## The dependent membership condition

`artinSymbol` is a *partial* construction: it takes an unramifiedness proof as an argument and has
no value at a ramified prime. So membership cannot be an equation between two total functions;
it is stated as

`∃ hur : (𝔭 is unramified in L), artinSymbol 𝔭.asIdeal hur = C`,

an existential over a proof. Membership is nonetheless unambiguous: it does not depend on which
unramifiedness proof witnesses it, and `mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_iff_artinSymbol_eq` turns the
existential into the plain equation `artinSymbol 𝔭.asIdeal hur = C` for whichever unramifiedness
proof `hur` the caller has in hand.

The alternative — a total `Gal(L/K)`-valued or `ConjClasses`-valued function taking a junk value
at the ramified primes — is worse for this set: the junk value carries no arithmetic content, yet
the ramified primes would sit inside the fibre of whichever class it names, so the fibres would
neither cover the unramified primes exactly nor be pinned down by a Frobenius element there. The
existential is what keeps the fibres free of them.

## Main definitions

* `NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPrimeSet`: the primes of `𝓞 K` unramified in `L` whose Artin
  class is `C`.

## Main results

* `NumberField.Chebotarev.mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_iff_artinSymbol_eq`: proof-independence — with
  any unramifiedness proof in hand, membership is the equation `artinSymbol 𝔭.asIdeal hur = C`.
* `NumberField.Chebotarev.mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_mk_iff_exists_isArithFrobAt`: for an unramified
  `𝔭` and an element `σ`, membership in the fibre of `[σ]` says exactly that `σ` is an arithmetic
  Frobenius at *some* prime of `𝓞 L` above `𝔭`.
* `NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPrimeSet_map_autCongr`: equivariance — an isomorphism
  `e : L ≃ₐ[K] L'` of extensions of `K` matches the fibre of `C` in `L` with the fibre in `L'` of
  the image of `C` under the induced isomorphism `AlgEquiv.autCongr e` of Galois groups.
* `NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPrimeSet_subset_map_restrictNormalHom`: a fibre over `L` lies
  in the fibre over a Galois subextension `M` of the restricted class.
* `NumberField.Chebotarev.disjoint_frobeniusPrimeSet`: distinct classes have disjoint fibres.
* `NumberField.Chebotarev.iUnion_frobeniusPrimeSet`: the fibres cover exactly the complement of
  `ramifiedPrimes K L`, so `existsUnique_mem_frobeniusPrimeSet` partitions the unramified primes
  and `finite_compl_iUnion_frobeniusPrimeSet` records that the discarded remainder is finite.

The last two are what let the density arguments discard a finite exceptional set and then work
one class at a time: a lower density bound for each class can be squeezed against a partition of
a cofinite set, which is how the crossing argument produces exact densities.

# The field cut out by an open normal subgroup of the absolute Galois group

Class field theory states its correspondences on the Galois side, as bijections between norm
subgroups and open normal subgroups `V` of the absolute Galois group
`G_F = Gal(Fˢ/F)`. This file records, once, the dictionary that turns such a subgroup back into a
field: the **class field** `classField F V` is the fixed field of `V` inside the separable closure
`Fˢ`. Because `G_F` is taken at the separable closure, the fixed field of all of `G_F` is `F`
itself, so no transport between closures intervenes.

By the infinite Galois correspondence the dictionary is faithful: the fixing subgroup of
`classField F V` is `V` again, `classField F V` is a finite Galois extension of `F` whose Galois
group is the finite quotient `G_F ⧸ V`, and every finite Galois subextension of `Fˢ` arises this
way. Subgroup inclusion becomes reverse inclusion of fields, which is how an order-preserving
correspondence on subgroups becomes the classical order-reversing correspondence on fields.
Finally `V` is an abelian layer exactly when its class field is an abelian extension.

## Main definitions

* `TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.classField F V`: the fixed field of `V` in `Fˢ`.
* `TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.galClassFieldEquiv`: the Galois group of `classField F V` over `F` is
  the Galois group of the finite normal layer `V ◁ G_F`.

## Main results

* `TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.fixingSubgroup_classField`: the fixing subgroup of the class field of
  `V` is `V`.
* `TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.classField_le_classField_iff`: `classField F W ≤ classField F V` if
  and only if `V ≤ W`.
* `TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.exists_classField_eq_iff`: the class fields are exactly the finite
  Galois subextensions of `Fˢ`.
* `TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.finrank_classField`: the degree of the class field of `V` is the index
  of `V`.
* `TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.isAbelianGalois_classField_iff`: the class field of `V` is abelian
  over `F` if and only if `V` is an abelian layer.

## References

* J. Neukirch, *Algebraic Number Theory*, Chapter IV, §1.
* J. Neukirch, A. Schmidt, K. Wingberg, *Cohomology of Number Fields*, 2nd ed., Chapter I, §1.

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction
declarations.doc:
An **ideal arithmetic function** over a field `K`: a complex-valued function on the nonzero
ideals of `𝓞 K`.

The domain is `(Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰`, Mathlib's non-zero-divisor submonoid. Since the ring of integers is
a domain, its elements are exactly the ideals different from `⊥`. For number fields, keeping `⊥`
out of the carrier ensures that later divisor sums use only the nonzero-ideal factorization
theory.
declarations.source: abbrev IdealArithmeticFunction := (Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰ → ℂ

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.IsMultiplicative
declarations.doc:
An ideal arithmetic function is multiplicative when it takes the unit ideal to `1` and
respects products of relatively prime nonzero ideals. This is weaker than the complete
multiplicativity carried by `MultiplicativeIdealWeight`.
declarations.source:
structure IsMultiplicative (f : IdealArithmeticFunction K) : Prop where
  /-- A multiplicative ideal arithmetic function takes the unit ideal to `1`. -/
  map_one : f 1 = 1
  /-- A multiplicative ideal arithmetic function respects products of relatively prime ideals. -/
  map_mul_of_isRelPrime {I J : (Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰}
    (hIJ : IsRelPrime (I : Ideal (𝓞 K)) (J : Ideal (𝓞 K))) : f (I * J) = f I * f J

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.isMultiplicative_one
declarations.doc: The everywhere-one ideal arithmetic function is multiplicative.
declarations.source: theorem isMultiplicative_one : IsMultiplicative (1 : IdealArithmeticFunction K)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.IsMultiplicative.mul
declarations.doc: Pointwise products of multiplicative ideal arithmetic functions are multiplicative.
declarations.source:
theorem IsMultiplicative.mul {f g : IdealArithmeticFunction K}
    (hf : f.IsMultiplicative) (hg : g.IsMultiplicative) : (f * g).IsMultiplicative

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.IsMultiplicative.star
declarations.doc: Complex conjugation preserves multiplicativity of ideal arithmetic functions.
declarations.source:
theorem IsMultiplicative.star {f : IdealArithmeticFunction K} (hf : f.IsMultiplicative) :
    (star f).IsMultiplicative

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.IsMultiplicative.map_prod
declarations.doc:
**A multiplicative ideal arithmetic function factors over pairwise relatively prime
products.** This is the ideal analogue of Mathlib's
`ArithmeticFunction.IsMultiplicative.map_prod`.

Passing from a pairwise hypothesis to relative primality against the whole product is exactly
Mathlib's `IsRelPrime.prod_right`, which needs `DecompositionMonoid (Ideal (𝓞 K))`; that is all
the ambient arithmetic this statement uses, and `[NumberField K]` supplies it.
declarations.source:
theorem IsMultiplicative.map_prod [DecompositionMonoid (Ideal (𝓞 K))] (hf : f.IsMultiplicative)
    {ι : Type*} (g : ι → (Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰)
    (s : Finset ι) (hs : (s : Set ι).Pairwise fun i j ↦ IsRelPrime (g i : Ideal (𝓞 K)) (g j)) :
    f (∏ i ∈ s, g i) = ∏ i ∈ s, f (g i)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.IsMultiplicative.map_prod_pow
declarations.doc:
**A multiplicative ideal arithmetic function factors over a prime-power factorization.**
Unique factorization writes every nonzero ideal as a product `∏ P ∈ S, P ^ e P` over a finite set
of height-one primes (`Ideal.exists_eq_prod_pow`), and a multiplicative `f` takes such a product to
the product of its values on the prime powers.
declarations.source:
theorem IsMultiplicative.map_prod_pow (hf : f.IsMultiplicative)
    (S : Finset (HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K))) (e : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K) → ℕ)
    (A : (Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰) (hA : (A : Ideal (𝓞 K)) = ∏ P ∈ S, P.asIdeal ^ e P) :
    f A = ∏ P ∈ S,
      f ⟨P.asIdeal ^ e P, mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_ne_zero (pow_ne_zero _ P.ne_bot)⟩

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.zeroExtend
declarations.doc:
Extend an ideal arithmetic function to all integral ideals by assigning zero to `⊥`.

Use `zeroExtend_bot` and `zeroExtend_coe` to simplify its two characteristic cases, rather than
unfolding this definition.
declarations.source:
noncomputable def zeroExtend (f : IdealArithmeticFunction K) : Ideal (𝓞 K) → ℂ := fun I =>
  Function.extend Subtype.val f 0 I

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.restrict
declarations.doc: Restrict a function on all integral ideals to the nonzero ideals.
declarations.source: def restrict (g : Ideal (𝓞 K) → ℂ) : IdealArithmeticFunction K := fun I => g I

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.restrict_apply
declarations.source: theorem restrict_apply (g : Ideal (𝓞 K) → ℂ) (I : (Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰) : restrict g I = g I

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.zeroExtend_bot
declarations.doc: The zero extension is zero at the zero ideal.
declarations.source: theorem zeroExtend_bot (f : IdealArithmeticFunction K) : f.zeroExtend ⊥ = 0

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.zeroExtend_of_ne
declarations.doc: Away from `⊥`, the zero extension is the original ideal arithmetic function.
declarations.source:
theorem zeroExtend_of_ne (f : IdealArithmeticFunction K) {I : Ideal (𝓞 K)} (hI : I ≠ ⊥) :
    f.zeroExtend I = f ⟨I, by simpa using hI⟩

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.zeroExtend_coe
declarations.doc: The zero extension agrees with the original function on every nonzero ideal.
declarations.source:
theorem zeroExtend_coe (f : IdealArithmeticFunction K) (I : (Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰) :
    f.zeroExtend I = f I

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.restrict_zeroExtend
declarations.doc: Restricting a zero extension recovers the original ideal arithmetic function.
declarations.source: theorem restrict_zeroExtend (f : IdealArithmeticFunction K) : restrict f.zeroExtend = f

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.zeroExtend_restrict
declarations.doc: Extending a restriction recovers a function on all ideals exactly when it vanishes at `⊥`.
declarations.source:
theorem zeroExtend_restrict {g : Ideal (𝓞 K) → ℂ} (hg : g ⊥ = 0) :
    (restrict g).zeroExtend = g

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.exists_zeroExtend_eq_iff
declarations.doc: A function on all ideals is a zero extension if and only if it vanishes at `⊥`.
declarations.source:
theorem exists_zeroExtend_eq_iff {g : Ideal (𝓞 K) → ℂ} :
    (∃ f : IdealArithmeticFunction K, f.zeroExtend = g) ↔ g ⊥ = 0

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.zeroExtend_injective
declarations.doc: Zero extension is injective: its values on nonzero ideals retain the entire function.
declarations.source:
theorem zeroExtend_injective :
    Function.Injective (zeroExtend : IdealArithmeticFunction K → Ideal (𝓞 K) → ℂ)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.zeroExtend_eq_iff
declarations.doc: Two zero extensions agree exactly when the underlying ideal arithmetic functions agree.
declarations.source:
theorem zeroExtend_eq_iff {f g : IdealArithmeticFunction K} :
    f.zeroExtend = g.zeroExtend ↔ f = g

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.existsUnique_zeroExtend_eq
declarations.doc:
A function on all ideals that vanishes at `⊥` is the zero extension of a unique ideal
arithmetic function.
declarations.source:
theorem existsUnique_zeroExtend_eq {g : Ideal (𝓞 K) → ℂ} (hg : g ⊥ = 0) :
    ∃! f : IdealArithmeticFunction K, f.zeroExtend = g

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.zeroExtend_eq_zero_iff
declarations.doc: The zero extension is zero exactly at `⊥` when the original function has no zero values.
declarations.source:
theorem zeroExtend_eq_zero_iff (f : IdealArithmeticFunction K)
    (hf : ∀ I, f I ≠ 0) {I : Ideal (𝓞 K)} : f.zeroExtend I = 0 ↔ I = ⊥

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.zeroExtend_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
If the original function does not vanish, its zero extension is nonzero at every nonzero
ideal.
declarations.source:
theorem zeroExtend_ne_zero (f : IdealArithmeticFunction K) (hf : ∀ I, f I ≠ 0)
    {I : Ideal (𝓞 K)} (hI : I ≠ ⊥) : f.zeroExtend I ≠ 0

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.zeroExtend_zero
declarations.doc: Zero extension preserves the pointwise zero function.
declarations.source: theorem zeroExtend_zero : zeroExtend (0 : IdealArithmeticFunction K) = 0

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.zeroExtend_add
declarations.doc: Zero extension preserves pointwise addition.
declarations.source:
theorem zeroExtend_add (f g : IdealArithmeticFunction K) :
    zeroExtend (f + g) = f.zeroExtend + g.zeroExtend

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.zeroExtend_neg
declarations.doc: Zero extension preserves pointwise negation.
declarations.source: theorem zeroExtend_neg (f : IdealArithmeticFunction K) : zeroExtend (-f) = -f.zeroExtend

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.zeroExtend_sub
declarations.doc: Zero extension preserves pointwise subtraction.
declarations.source:
theorem zeroExtend_sub (f g : IdealArithmeticFunction K) :
    zeroExtend (f - g) = f.zeroExtend - g.zeroExtend

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.zeroExtend_smul
declarations.doc: Zero extension preserves pointwise complex scalar multiplication.
declarations.source:
theorem zeroExtend_smul (c : ℂ) (f : IdealArithmeticFunction K) :
    zeroExtend (c • f) = c • f.zeroExtend

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.zeroExtend_mul
declarations.doc: Zero extension preserves pointwise multiplication.
declarations.source:
theorem zeroExtend_mul (f g : IdealArithmeticFunction K) :
    zeroExtend (f * g) = f.zeroExtend * g.zeroExtend

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.not_exists_zeroExtend_eq_one
declarations.doc:
**Rejection test.** The everywhere-one function on *all* integral ideals is not the zero
extension of any ideal arithmetic function, since its value at `⊥` is one rather than zero. This
is the roadmap's zero-ideal rejection test. Compare
`TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.zeroExtend_one_apply`, which computes the zero extension of the
constant function `1` on the *nonzero* ideals.
declarations.source:
theorem not_exists_zeroExtend_eq_one :
    ¬ ∃ f : IdealArithmeticFunction K, f.zeroExtend = (1 : Ideal (𝓞 K) → ℂ)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.zeroExtend_one_apply
declarations.doc:
The constant-one function on nonzero ideals extends to the indicator of ideals unequal to
`⊥`.
declarations.source:
theorem zeroExtend_one_apply (I : Ideal (𝓞 K)) :
    (1 : IdealArithmeticFunction K).zeroExtend I = if I = ⊥ then 0 else 1

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.map
declarations.doc:
**Transport along an isomorphism of fields.** An isomorphism `e : K ≃+* L` carries an ideal
arithmetic function for `K` to one for `L`: the value at a nonzero ideal of `𝓞 L` is the value
of `f` at its preimage in `𝓞 K` under `NumberField.RingOfIntegers.mapRingEquiv e`.
declarations.source:
noncomputable def map (e : K ≃+* L) (f : IdealArithmeticFunction K) :
    IdealArithmeticFunction L := fun J ↦
  f.zeroExtend (Ideal.comap (RingOfIntegers.mapRingEquiv e) (J : Ideal (𝓞 L)))

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.map_apply
declarations.doc:
Defining equation of `TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.map`: the value at a nonzero ideal
of `𝓞 L` is the zero extension of `f` at its preimage in `𝓞 K`.
declarations.source:
theorem map_apply (e : K ≃+* L) (f : IdealArithmeticFunction K) (J : (Ideal (𝓞 L))⁰) :
    map e f J = f.zeroExtend (Ideal.comap (RingOfIntegers.mapRingEquiv e) (J : Ideal (𝓞 L)))

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.zeroExtend_map
declarations.doc:
**Transport is compatible with extension by zero**: both extensions send an ideal of `𝓞 L`
to the value of `f` at its preimage in `𝓞 K`, the zero ideal included.
declarations.source:
theorem zeroExtend_map (e : K ≃+* L) (f : IdealArithmeticFunction K) (I : Ideal (𝓞 L)) :
    (map e f).zeroExtend I =
      f.zeroExtend (Ideal.comap (RingOfIntegers.mapRingEquiv e) I)

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.map_id
declarations.doc: Transporting along the identity field isomorphism is the identity.
declarations.source: theorem map_id (f : IdealArithmeticFunction K) : map (RingEquiv.refl K) f = f

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.map_map
declarations.doc:
**Transport is functorial**: transporting along `e` and then along `e'` is the same as
transporting along `e.trans e'`.
declarations.source:
theorem map_map (e : K ≃+* L) (e' : L ≃+* M) (f : IdealArithmeticFunction K) :
    map e' (map e f) = map (e.trans e') f

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.mapEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Transport along an isomorphism of fields, as an equivalence** of the two carriers, with
inverse the transport along `e.symm`.
declarations.source:
noncomputable def mapEquiv (e : K ≃+* L) :
    IdealArithmeticFunction K ≃ IdealArithmeticFunction L where
  toFun := map e
  invFun := map e.symm
  left_inv f := by rw [map_map, e.self_trans_symm, map_id]
  right_inv f := by rw [map_map, e.symm_trans_self, map_id]

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.mapEquiv_apply
declarations.doc: Evaluation of `mapEquiv`.
declarations.source:
theorem mapEquiv_apply (e : K ≃+* L) (f : IdealArithmeticFunction K) :
    mapEquiv e f = map e f

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.mapEquiv_symm_apply
declarations.doc: Evaluation of the inverse of `mapEquiv`.
declarations.source:
theorem mapEquiv_symm_apply (e : K ≃+* L) (f : IdealArithmeticFunction L) :
    (mapEquiv e).symm f = map e.symm f

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.map_zero
declarations.doc: Transport preserves the pointwise zero function.
declarations.source: theorem map_zero (e : K ≃+* L) : map e (0 : IdealArithmeticFunction K) = 0

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.map_one
declarations.doc: Transport preserves the pointwise one function.
declarations.source: theorem map_one (e : K ≃+* L) : map e (1 : IdealArithmeticFunction K) = 1

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.map_add
declarations.doc: Transport preserves pointwise addition.
declarations.source:
theorem map_add (e : K ≃+* L) (f g : IdealArithmeticFunction K) :
    map e (f + g) = map e f + map e g

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.map_mul
declarations.doc: Transport preserves pointwise multiplication.
declarations.source:
theorem map_mul (e : K ≃+* L) (f g : IdealArithmeticFunction K) :
    map e (f * g) = map e f * map e g

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.map_neg
declarations.doc: Transport preserves pointwise negation.
declarations.source: theorem map_neg (e : K ≃+* L) (f : IdealArithmeticFunction K) : map e (-f) = -map e f

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.map_sub
declarations.doc: Transport preserves pointwise subtraction.
declarations.source:
theorem map_sub (e : K ≃+* L) (f g : IdealArithmeticFunction K) :
    map e (f - g) = map e f - map e g

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.map_smul
declarations.doc: Transport preserves pointwise complex scalar multiplication.
declarations.source:
theorem map_smul (e : K ≃+* L) (c : ℂ) (f : IdealArithmeticFunction K) :
    map e (c • f) = c • map e f

declarations.name: TauCeti.one_lt_absNorm_of_prime
declarations.doc: The absolute norm of a prime ideal is greater than one.
declarations.source:
theorem one_lt_absNorm_of_prime {P : Ideal (𝓞 K)} (hP : Prime P) :
    1 < Ideal.absNorm P

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt
declarations.doc:
The **ideal von Mangoldt function**.  It takes the value `log N(P)` on every positive power of
a prime ideal `P`, and vanishes on ideals which are not prime powers.

The codomain is `ℂ`, matching `IdealArithmeticFunction`, although every value is real.
declarations.source:
noncomputable def vonMangoldt : IdealArithmeticFunction K := fun A ↦
  if h : IsPrimePow (A : Ideal (𝓞 K)) then
    (Real.log (Ideal.absNorm h.choose) : ℂ)
  else 0

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt_one
declarations.doc: The ideal von Mangoldt function vanishes at the unit ideal.
declarations.source: theorem vonMangoldt_one : (vonMangoldt : IdealArithmeticFunction K) 1 = 0

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt_apply_of_eq_prime_pow
declarations.doc:
The value of the ideal von Mangoldt function at a positive power of a prime ideal.  This is the
choice-free characterization of `vonMangoldt` on its support.

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt_apply_prime_pow
declarations.doc: The ideal von Mangoldt function at a positive power of a prime nonzero ideal.
declarations.source:
theorem vonMangoldt_apply_prime_pow {P : (Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰}
    (hP : Prime (P : Ideal (𝓞 K))) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) :
    (vonMangoldt : IdealArithmeticFunction K) (P ^ n) =
      Real.log (Ideal.absNorm (P : Ideal (𝓞 K)))

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt_apply_prime
declarations.doc: The ideal von Mangoldt function at a prime ideal.
declarations.source:
theorem vonMangoldt_apply_prime {P : (Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰}
    (hP : Prime (P : Ideal (𝓞 K))) :
    (vonMangoldt : IdealArithmeticFunction K) P =
      Real.log (Ideal.absNorm (P : Ideal (𝓞 K)))

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt_eq_zero_of_not_isPrimePow
declarations.doc: The ideal von Mangoldt function vanishes away from prime powers.

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt_ne_zero_iff
declarations.doc: The support of the ideal von Mangoldt function is exactly the set of prime-power ideals.
declarations.source:
theorem vonMangoldt_ne_zero_iff {A : (Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰} :
    (vonMangoldt : IdealArithmeticFunction K) A ≠ 0 ↔ IsPrimePow (A : Ideal (𝓞 K))

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt_eq_zero_iff
declarations.doc: The ideal von Mangoldt function vanishes exactly away from prime powers.
declarations.source:
theorem vonMangoldt_eq_zero_iff {A : (Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰} :
    (vonMangoldt : IdealArithmeticFunction K) A = 0 ↔ ¬ IsPrimePow (A : Ideal (𝓞 K))

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt_im
declarations.doc: Every value of the ideal von Mangoldt function is real.
declarations.source:
theorem vonMangoldt_im {A : (Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰} :
    ((vonMangoldt : IdealArithmeticFunction K) A).im = 0

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt_re_nonneg
declarations.doc: The (real) values of the ideal von Mangoldt function are nonnegative.
declarations.source:
theorem vonMangoldt_re_nonneg {A : (Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰} :
    0 ≤ ((vonMangoldt : IdealArithmeticFunction K) A).re

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.norm_vonMangoldt_le_log
declarations.doc:
**The von Mangoldt function is bounded by the logarithm of the norm.** On a power `P ^ n` its
value is `log N(P)`, and the norm of the ideal is `N(P) ^ n` with `n ≥ 1`, so the bound is the
inequality `log N(P) ≤ n log N(P)`; off the prime powers the function vanishes and the logarithm is
still nonnegative.

This is the ideal analogue of `ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt_le_log`, and it is what compares a
von Mangoldt weighted ideal term against the `log N(I)` weighted terms of
`TauCeti.summable_log_absNorm_mul_norm_idealTerm_of_re_lt_re`.
declarations.source:
theorem norm_vonMangoldt_le_log (A : (Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰) :
    ‖(vonMangoldt : IdealArithmeticFunction K) A‖
      ≤ Real.log (Ideal.absNorm (A : Ideal (𝓞 K)))

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldtTransform
declarations.doc:
The **von Mangoldt transform** of an ideal arithmetic function `f`: the pointwise product
`A ↦ f(A) Λ(A)`.
declarations.source:
noncomputable def vonMangoldtTransform (f : IdealArithmeticFunction K) :
    IdealArithmeticFunction K :=
  f * vonMangoldt

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldtTransform_apply
declarations.doc: Evaluation of the von Mangoldt transform.
declarations.source:
theorem vonMangoldtTransform_apply (f : IdealArithmeticFunction K)
    (A : (Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰) :
    f.vonMangoldtTransform A = f A * vonMangoldt A

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldtTransform_apply_prime_pow
declarations.doc: The von Mangoldt transform on a positive power of a prime ideal.
declarations.source:
theorem vonMangoldtTransform_apply_prime_pow (f : IdealArithmeticFunction K)
    {P : (Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰} (hP : Prime (P : Ideal (𝓞 K))) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) :
    f.vonMangoldtTransform (P ^ n) =
      f (P ^ n) * Real.log (Ideal.absNorm (P : Ideal (𝓞 K)))

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldtTransform_ne_zero_iff
declarations.doc:
The support of a von Mangoldt transform is the intersection of the support of the original
function with the prime-power ideals.
declarations.source:
theorem vonMangoldtTransform_ne_zero_iff (f : IdealArithmeticFunction K)
    {A : (Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰} :
    f.vonMangoldtTransform A ≠ 0 ↔
      IsPrimePow (A : Ideal (𝓞 K)) ∧ f A ≠ 0

declarations.name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldtTransform_one
declarations.doc:
The transform of the constant-one ideal arithmetic function is the ideal von Mangoldt
function.
declarations.source:
theorem vonMangoldtTransform_one :
    (1 : IdealArithmeticFunction K).vonMangoldtTransform = vonMangoldt

declarations.name: TauCeti.MultiplicativeIdealWeight.vonMangoldtTransform_apply_prime_pow
declarations.doc:
The von Mangoldt transform of a completely multiplicative weight on a positive power of a
prime ideal.
declarations.source:
theorem vonMangoldtTransform_apply_prime_pow (χ : MultiplicativeIdealWeight K)
    {P : (Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰} (hP : Prime (P : Ideal (𝓞 K))) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) :
    χ.toIdealArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldtTransform (P ^ n) =
      χ P ^ n * Real.log (Ideal.absNorm (P : Ideal (𝓞 K)))

declarations.name: TauCeti.MultiplicativeIdealWeight.vonMangoldtTransform_ne_zero_iff
declarations.doc:
The support of the von Mangoldt transform of a completely multiplicative weight consists
exactly of the prime powers on which the weight is good.
declarations.source:
theorem vonMangoldtTransform_ne_zero_iff (χ : MultiplicativeIdealWeight K)
    {A : (Ideal (𝓞 K))⁰} :
    χ.toIdealArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldtTransform A ≠ 0 ↔
      IsPrimePow (A : Ideal (𝓞 K)) ∧ χ.IsGood (A : Ideal (𝓞 K))

declarations.name: NumberField.Set.HasNaturalDensity
declarations.doc:
A set `S` of height-one primes of a number field has natural density `δ` when the proportion
of primes of `S` below `x`, relative to all primes below `x`, tends to `δ` as `x → ∞`.

Both counts use the inclusive real cutoff fixed by `TauCeti.primeCount`.

declarations.name: NumberField.Set.hasNaturalDensity_def
declarations.doc: Unfolds `HasNaturalDensity` to the convergence of the ratio of prime counts.
declarations.source:
theorem hasNaturalDensity_def :
    HasNaturalDensity S δ ↔ Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => TauCeti.primeCount K S x /
      TauCeti.primeCount K (Set.univ : Set (HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K))) x) atTop (𝓝 δ)

declarations.name: NumberField.Set.HasNaturalDensity.unique
declarations.doc: A set of prime ideals has at most one natural density.
declarations.source:
theorem HasNaturalDensity.unique (hδ : HasNaturalDensity S δ) (hε : HasNaturalDensity S ε) :
    δ = ε

declarations.name: NumberField.Set.hasNaturalDensity_empty
declarations.doc: The empty set of prime ideals has natural density zero.
declarations.source:
theorem hasNaturalDensity_empty :
    HasNaturalDensity (∅ : Set (HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K))) 0

declarations.name: NumberField.Set.hasNaturalDensity_univ
declarations.doc: The set of all prime ideals has natural density one.
declarations.source:
theorem hasNaturalDensity_univ :
    HasNaturalDensity (Set.univ : Set (HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K))) 1

declarations.name: NumberField.Set.HasNaturalDensity.nonneg
declarations.doc: A natural density is nonnegative.
declarations.source: theorem HasNaturalDensity.nonneg (h : HasNaturalDensity S δ) : 0 ≤ δ

declarations.name: NumberField.Set.HasNaturalDensity.le_one
declarations.doc: A natural density is at most one.
declarations.source: theorem HasNaturalDensity.le_one (h : HasNaturalDensity S δ) : δ ≤ 1

declarations.name: NumberField.Set.HasNaturalDensity.mono
declarations.doc: Inclusion of prime sets orders their natural densities, when both densities exist.
declarations.source:
theorem HasNaturalDensity.mono (hST : S ⊆ T) (hS : HasNaturalDensity S δ)
    (hT : HasNaturalDensity T ε) : δ ≤ ε

declarations.name: NumberField.Set.HasNaturalDensity.union
declarations.doc: Natural density is additive on disjoint unions of prime sets.
declarations.source:
theorem HasNaturalDensity.union (hS : HasNaturalDensity S δ) (hT : HasNaturalDensity T ε)
    (hST : Disjoint S T) : HasNaturalDensity (S ∪ T) (δ + ε)

declarations.name: NumberField.Set.hasNaturalDensity_biUnion_finset
declarations.doc: Natural density is additive on a finite family of pairwise disjoint prime sets.

declarations.name: NumberField.Set.HasNaturalDensity.compl
declarations.doc: The complement of a set of natural density `δ` has natural density `1 - δ`.
declarations.source:
theorem HasNaturalDensity.compl (hS : HasNaturalDensity S δ) :
    HasNaturalDensity Sᶜ (1 - δ)

declarations.name: NumberField.Set.HasNaturalDensity.of_finite_symmDiff
declarations.doc: Changing a set on finitely many prime ideals preserves its natural density.
declarations.source:
theorem HasNaturalDensity.of_finite_symmDiff (hT : HasNaturalDensity T δ)
    (hST : (symmDiff S T).Finite) : HasNaturalDensity S δ

declarations.name: NumberField.Set.hasNaturalDensity_iff_of_finite_symmDiff
declarations.doc: Two prime sets with finite symmetric difference have natural density `δ` simultaneously.
declarations.source:
theorem hasNaturalDensity_iff_of_finite_symmDiff (hST : (symmDiff S T).Finite) :
    HasNaturalDensity S δ ↔ HasNaturalDensity T δ

declarations.name: NumberField.Set.hasNaturalDensity_of_finite
declarations.doc: Every finite set of prime ideals has natural density zero.
declarations.source: theorem hasNaturalDensity_of_finite (hS : S.Finite) : HasNaturalDensity S 0

declarations.name: NumberField.Set.isUpperDirichletDensityBound_of_eventually_primeCount_le
declarations.doc:
**Upper natural bounds are upper Dirichlet bounds.** If eventually at most the proportion `c`
of the primes of norm at most `x` lie in `S`, then `c` is an upper Dirichlet-density bound for
`S`.

declarations.name: NumberField.Set.isLowerDirichletDensityBound_of_eventually_le_primeCount
declarations.doc:
**Lower natural bounds are lower Dirichlet bounds.** If eventually at least the proportion `c`
of the primes of norm at most `x` lie in `S`, then `c` is a lower Dirichlet-density bound for
`S`.

declarations.name: NumberField.Set.hasDirichletDensity_of_hasNaturalDensity
declarations.doc:
**Natural density implies Dirichlet density.** A set of prime ideals with natural density `δ`
has Dirichlet density `δ`.
declarations.source:
theorem hasDirichletDensity_of_hasNaturalDensity (h : HasNaturalDensity S δ) :
    HasDirichletDensity S δ

declarations.name: NumberField.Chebotarev.mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_one_iff_inertiaDeg_eq_one
declarations.doc:
**The identity fibre is residue degree one.** For `𝔭` unramified in `L` and `Q` a prime of
`𝓞 L` above `𝔭`, the prime `𝔭` carries the identity Artin class exactly when `f(Q/𝔭) = 1`.

The residue degree is common to all primes above `𝔭`, so the choice of `Q` is immaterial; see
`inertiaDeg_eq_one_of_mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_one`.
declarations.source:
theorem mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_one_iff_inertiaDeg_eq_one {𝔭 : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)}
    (hur : ∀ (Q : Ideal (𝓞 L)) [Q.IsPrime] [Q.LiesOver 𝔭.asIdeal],
      Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt (𝓞 K) Q) (Q : Ideal (𝓞 L)) [Q.IsPrime] [Q.LiesOver 𝔭.asIdeal] :
    𝔭 ∈ frobeniusPrimeSet K L 1 ↔ Q.inertiaDeg (𝓞 K) = 1

declarations.name: NumberField.Chebotarev.mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_one_iff_ncard_primesOver_eq_finrank
declarations.source:
theorem mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_one_iff_ncard_primesOver_eq_finrank
    {𝔭 : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)} :
    𝔭 ∈ frobeniusPrimeSet K L 1 ↔ (𝔭.asIdeal.primesOver (𝓞 L)).ncard = Module.finrank K L

declarations.name: NumberField.Chebotarev.inertiaDeg_eq_one_of_mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_one
declarations.doc:
**Residue degree one at every prime above.** A member of the identity fibre has residue
degree `1` at each prime of `𝓞 L` lying over it, not merely at one of them.

declarations.name: NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPrimeSet_one_eq_setOf_ncard_primesOver_eq_finrank
declarations.doc:
**The identity fibre is exactly the completely split primes.** A height-one prime of `𝓞 K`
carries the identity Artin class in `L` if and only if `𝓞 L` has `[L : K]` primes above it.

Complete splitting is therefore a fibre of the Artin class with no exceptional set attached, so
a density statement for the fibre is a density statement for the completely split primes.
declarations.source:
theorem frobeniusPrimeSet_one_eq_setOf_ncard_primesOver_eq_finrank :
    frobeniusPrimeSet K L 1 = {𝔭 | (𝔭.asIdeal.primesOver (𝓞 L)).ncard = Module.finrank K L}

declarations.name: NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPrimeSet
declarations.doc:
**The primes of `K` with Artin class `C` in `L`.** A height-one prime `𝔭` of `𝓞 K` belongs to
`frobeniusPrimeSet K L C` when `𝔭` is unramified in `L` — so that `artinSymbol` is applicable —
and its Artin class is `C`.

The unramifiedness proof is packaged existentially rather than assumed, because `artinSymbol`
takes it as an argument and no value is assigned at a ramified prime. See
`mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_iff_artinSymbol_eq` for the form used once such a proof is available.

The carrier and this membership condition are taken from
`TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev/Suggested.lean`, lines 64–76, described in the section
`Frobenius prime sets and finite exceptional sets` of `TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev/README.md`.

declarations.name: NumberField.Chebotarev.mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_iff
declarations.doc:
Membership in `frobeniusPrimeSet`, unfolded. Downstream files should open the definition
through this lemma rather than through defeq.
declarations.source:
theorem mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_iff {𝔭 : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)}
    {C : ConjClasses (L ≃ₐ[K] L)} :
    𝔭 ∈ frobeniusPrimeSet K L C ↔
      ∃ hur : ∀ (Q : Ideal (𝓞 L)) [Q.IsPrime] [Q.LiesOver 𝔭.asIdeal],
        Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt (𝓞 K) Q, artinSymbol 𝔭.asIdeal hur = C

declarations.name: NumberField.Chebotarev.mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_iff_artinSymbol_eq
declarations.doc:
**Proof-independence.** Once an unramifiedness proof `hur` is available, membership in
`frobeniusPrimeSet K L C` is the plain equation `artinSymbol 𝔭.asIdeal hur = C`: the existential
in the definition may be instantiated at `hur`, whatever proof it was introduced with.

Membership in `frobeniusPrimeSet K L C` is therefore independent of the unramifiedness proof used
to test it.
declarations.source:
theorem mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_iff_artinSymbol_eq {𝔭 : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)}
    (hur : ∀ (Q : Ideal (𝓞 L)) [Q.IsPrime] [Q.LiesOver 𝔭.asIdeal],
      Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt (𝓞 K) Q) (C : ConjClasses (L ≃ₐ[K] L)) :
    𝔭 ∈ frobeniusPrimeSet K L C ↔ artinSymbol 𝔭.asIdeal hur = C

declarations.name: NumberField.Chebotarev.mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_artinSymbol
declarations.doc: An unramified prime lies in the fibre of its own Artin class.
declarations.source:
theorem mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_artinSymbol {𝔭 : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)}
    (hur : ∀ (Q : Ideal (𝓞 L)) [Q.IsPrime] [Q.LiesOver 𝔭.asIdeal],
      Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt (𝓞 K) Q) :
    𝔭 ∈ frobeniusPrimeSet K L (artinSymbol 𝔭.asIdeal hur)

declarations.name: NumberField.Chebotarev.isUnramifiedAt_of_mem_frobeniusPrimeSet
declarations.doc: A member of `frobeniusPrimeSet K L C` is unramified in `L`.
declarations.source:
theorem isUnramifiedAt_of_mem_frobeniusPrimeSet {𝔭 : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)}
    {C : ConjClasses (L ≃ₐ[K] L)} (h : 𝔭 ∈ frobeniusPrimeSet K L C)
    (Q : Ideal (𝓞 L)) [Q.IsPrime] [Q.LiesOver 𝔭.asIdeal] :
    Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt (𝓞 K) Q

declarations.name: NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPrimeSet_subset_compl_ramifiedPrimes
declarations.doc: No ramified prime carries an Artin class: the fibres avoid `ramifiedPrimes K L`.
declarations.source:
theorem frobeniusPrimeSet_subset_compl_ramifiedPrimes (C : ConjClasses (L ≃ₐ[K] L)) :
    frobeniusPrimeSet K L C ⊆ (↑(ramifiedPrimes K L))ᶜ

declarations.name: NumberField.Chebotarev.mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_mk_of_isArithFrobAt
declarations.doc:
**A Frobenius witnesses membership.** If `σ` is an arithmetic Frobenius at a prime `Q` of
`𝓞 L` above an unramified `𝔭`, then `𝔭` lies in the fibre of the class of `σ`.

declarations.name: NumberField.Chebotarev.exists_isArithFrobAt_of_mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_mk
declarations.doc:
**Every representative is realized.** If `𝔭` lies in the fibre of the class of `σ`, then `σ`
itself — not merely some conjugate of it — is an arithmetic Frobenius at some prime of `𝓞 L`
above `𝔭`.

declarations.name: NumberField.Chebotarev.mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_mk_iff_exists_isArithFrobAt
declarations.doc:
**The fibre of a class, read off from any one representative.** For `𝔭` unramified in `L`,
membership in the fibre of `[σ]` says exactly that `σ` is an arithmetic Frobenius at some prime
of `𝓞 L` above `𝔭`.
declarations.source:
theorem mem_frobeniusPrimeSet_mk_iff_exists_isArithFrobAt {𝔭 : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)}
    (hur : ∀ (Q : Ideal (𝓞 L)) [Q.IsPrime] [Q.LiesOver 𝔭.asIdeal],
      Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt (𝓞 K) Q) (σ : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
    𝔭 ∈ frobeniusPrimeSet K L (ConjClasses.mk σ) ↔
      ∃ Q : 𝔭.asIdeal.primesOver (𝓞 L), IsArithFrobAt (𝓞 K) σ Q.1

declarations.name: NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPrimeSet_map_autCongr
declarations.doc:
**Equivariance under an isomorphism of extensions.** An isomorphism `e : L ≃ₐ[K] L'` carries
the fibre of `C` over `L` onto the fibre over `L'` of the image of `C` under the induced
isomorphism `AlgEquiv.autCongr e` of Galois groups.

So the fibres depend only on the extension `L / K` up to isomorphism, not on the model of `L`
chosen to compute the Artin symbol.
declarations.source:
theorem frobeniusPrimeSet_map_autCongr (C : ConjClasses (L ≃ₐ[K] L)) (e : L ≃ₐ[K] L') :
    frobeniusPrimeSet K L' (ConjClasses.map (AlgEquiv.autCongr e).toMonoidHom C) =
      frobeniusPrimeSet K L C

declarations.name: NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPrimeSet_subset_map_restrictNormalHom
declarations.doc:
**Fibres shrink along restriction to a normal subextension.** For a tower `L / M / K` with
`M / K` Galois, a prime in the fibre of `C` over `L` lies in the fibre over `M` of the restriction
of `C`. Unramifiedness in `M` is part of the conclusion, not a hypothesis.

This is `artinSymbol_map_restrictNormalHom` read on fibres: restriction takes no power.
declarations.source:
theorem frobeniusPrimeSet_subset_map_restrictNormalHom (C : ConjClasses (L ≃ₐ[K] L)) :
    frobeniusPrimeSet K L C ⊆
      frobeniusPrimeSet K M (ConjClasses.map (AlgEquiv.restrictNormalHom M) C)

declarations.name: NumberField.Chebotarev.disjoint_frobeniusPrimeSet
declarations.doc: **Distinct classes have disjoint fibres.** A prime unramified in `L` has one Artin class.
declarations.source:
theorem disjoint_frobeniusPrimeSet {C D : ConjClasses (L ≃ₐ[K] L)} (h : C ≠ D) :
    Disjoint (frobeniusPrimeSet K L C) (frobeniusPrimeSet K L D)

declarations.name: NumberField.Chebotarev.pairwise_disjoint_frobeniusPrimeSet
declarations.doc: The fibres of the Artin class are pairwise disjoint.
declarations.source:
theorem pairwise_disjoint_frobeniusPrimeSet :
    Pairwise (Function.onFun Disjoint (frobeniusPrimeSet K L))

declarations.name: NumberField.Chebotarev.iUnion_frobeniusPrimeSet
declarations.doc:
**The fibres cover the unramified primes.** The union of the Artin fibres over all conjugacy
classes of `Gal(L/K)` is exactly the complement of the finite set `ramifiedPrimes K L`.

Together with `disjoint_frobeniusPrimeSet` this is the partition that the density arguments run
on: everything outside a finite exceptional set is accounted for exactly once.
declarations.source:
theorem iUnion_frobeniusPrimeSet :
    ⋃ C : ConjClasses (L ≃ₐ[K] L), frobeniusPrimeSet K L C = (↑(ramifiedPrimes K L))ᶜ

declarations.name: NumberField.Chebotarev.existsUnique_mem_frobeniusPrimeSet
declarations.doc:
**The Artin class partitions the unramified primes.** A prime of `𝓞 K` outside
`ramifiedPrimes K L` lies in the fibre of exactly one conjugacy class of `Gal(L/K)`.

declarations.name: NumberField.Chebotarev.finite_compl_iUnion_frobeniusPrimeSet
declarations.doc:
**The uncovered set is finite.** Only finitely many primes of `𝓞 K` fail to lie in some Artin
fibre, so a density statement may discard them.
declarations.source:
theorem finite_compl_iUnion_frobeniusPrimeSet :
    (⋃ C : ConjClasses (L ≃ₐ[K] L), frobeniusPrimeSet K L C)ᶜ.Finite

declarations.name: TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.classField
declarations.doc:
**The class field of an open normal subgroup** `V` of the absolute Galois group `G_F`: the
fixed field of `V` inside the separable closure of `F`. It is the finite Galois extension of `F`
with Galois group `G_F ⧸ V`.

declarations.name: TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.mem_classField
declarations.doc:
An element of `Fˢ` lies in the class field of `V` exactly when every element of `V` fixes
it.
declarations.source:
theorem mem_classField {V : OpenNormalSubgroup (AbsoluteGaloisGroup F)} {x : SeparableClosure F} :
    x ∈ classField F V ↔ ∀ σ ∈ V, σ x = x

declarations.name: TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.fixingSubgroup_classField
declarations.doc:
The fixing subgroup of the class field of `V` is `V`: an open subgroup is closed, so the
infinite Galois correspondence recovers it from its fixed field.
declarations.source:
theorem fixingSubgroup_classField (V : OpenNormalSubgroup (AbsoluteGaloisGroup F)) :
    (classField F V).fixingSubgroup = V.toSubgroup

declarations.name: TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.classField_le_classField_iff
declarations.doc:
**The Galois dictionary reverses inclusions**: a larger subgroup cuts out a smaller field.
This turns a class-field correspondence that preserves the order on subgroups into the classical
order-reversing correspondence on fields.
declarations.source:
theorem classField_le_classField_iff (V W : OpenNormalSubgroup (AbsoluteGaloisGroup F)) :
    classField F W ≤ classField F V ↔ V ≤ W

declarations.name: TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.classField_injective
declarations.doc: Distinct open normal subgroups cut out distinct class fields.
declarations.source: theorem classField_injective : Function.Injective (classField F)

declarations.name: TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.classField_eq_bot_iff
declarations.doc: The class field of `V` is `F` exactly when `V` is the whole absolute Galois group.
declarations.source:
theorem classField_eq_bot_iff {V : OpenNormalSubgroup (AbsoluteGaloisGroup F)} :
    classField F V = ⊥ ↔ V.toSubgroup = ⊤

declarations.name: TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.exists_classField_eq_iff
declarations.doc: **The class fields are exactly the finite Galois subextensions of `Fˢ`.**
declarations.source:
theorem exists_classField_eq_iff (L : IntermediateField F (SeparableClosure F)) :
    (∃ V, classField F V = L) ↔ FiniteDimensional F L ∧ IsGalois F L

declarations.name: TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.finrank_classField
declarations.doc: **The degree of the class field of `V` is the index of `V`.**
declarations.source:
theorem finrank_classField (V : OpenNormalSubgroup (AbsoluteGaloisGroup F)) :
    Module.finrank F (classField F V) = V.toSubgroup.index

declarations.name: TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.galClassFieldEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The Galois group of a class field is the Galois group of its layer**: restriction to
`classField F V` identifies `Gal(classField F V / F)` with the finite Galois group `G_F ⧸ V` of
the normal layer `V ◁ G_F`.
declarations.source:
def galClassFieldEquiv (V : OpenNormalSubgroup (AbsoluteGaloisGroup F)) :
    Gal(classField F V/F) ≃* (NormalLayer.ofOpenNormal V).Gal :=
  have : (⟨V.toSubgroup, V.toOpenSubgroup.isClosed⟩ :
      ClosedSubgroup (AbsoluteGaloisGroup F)).Normal := V.isNormal'
  ((NormalLayer.galOfOpenNormalEquiv V).trans
    (InfiniteGalois.normalAutEquivQuotient ⟨V.toSubgroup, V.toOpenSubgroup.isClosed⟩ :
      AbsoluteGaloisGroup F ⧸ V.toSubgroup ≃* Gal(classField F V/F))).symm

declarations.name: TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.galClassFieldEquiv_symm_mk
declarations.doc:
The inverse of `galClassFieldEquiv` sends the class of `σ ∈ G_F` to the restriction of `σ` to
the class field.
declarations.source:
theorem galClassFieldEquiv_symm_mk (V : OpenNormalSubgroup (AbsoluteGaloisGroup F))
    (σ : (NormalLayer.ofOpenNormal V).ground) :
    (galClassFieldEquiv V).symm (QuotientGroup.mk σ) =
      AlgEquiv.restrictNormalHom (classField F V) (σ : AbsoluteGaloisGroup F)

declarations.name: TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.galOfOpenNormalEquiv_galClassFieldEquiv_restrictNormalHom
declarations.doc:
Read in `G_F ⧸ V`, `galClassFieldEquiv` sends the restriction of `σ ∈ G_F` to the class field
to the class of `σ`.
declarations.source:
theorem galOfOpenNormalEquiv_galClassFieldEquiv_restrictNormalHom
    (V : OpenNormalSubgroup (AbsoluteGaloisGroup F)) (σ : AbsoluteGaloisGroup F) :
    NormalLayer.galOfOpenNormalEquiv V
        (galClassFieldEquiv V (AlgEquiv.restrictNormalHom (classField F V) σ)) =
      (σ : AbsoluteGaloisGroup F ⧸ V.toSubgroup)

declarations.name: TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.isAbelianGalois_classField_iff
declarations.doc: **The class field of `V` is abelian over `F` exactly when `V` is an abelian layer.**
declarations.source:
theorem isAbelianGalois_classField_iff {V : OpenNormalSubgroup (AbsoluteGaloisGroup F)} :
    IsAbelianGalois F (classField F V) ↔ V.IsAbelianClassFieldLayer
